The Popular Diet Linked to an Older Biological Age (with Dr. Guru Banavar)
articles.description:
#nutrition #microbiome #aihealthcare 

In Episode #1043, Dr. Guru Banavar (Founding CTO of Viome) joins @JonKrohnLearns for a technical masterclass on the biology inside your gut. Viome has assembled what Guru calls the largest dataset on human biology ever collected, roughly 100 quadrillion nucleotides of RNA from people in more than 150 countries, and uses it to tell individuals which foods help them and which harm them. Before Viome, Guru was the first VP to lead IBM's Watson AI team, and he holds a PhD in computer science from the University of Utah. In this episode, he explains why RNA rather than DNA holds the key to chronic disease, how a continuous-glucose study of 1,100 people became a predictive model for your blood sugar, why keto dieters come out biologically older than vegetarians, and what makes computational biology such a rare skill.

310: The Automation Skills Gap: Why Manufacturers Need to Train the Workforce They Already Have
articles.description:
Five years ago, many companies treated training as optional. That’s changing.

Joining Chris is Christelle Keefer, Director of Training and Certification at the Association for Advancing Automation (A3), back for a second visit. Before she started at A3, she spent years at a robotics OEM working with schools, instructors, and customers worldwide. And if she had her way, this conversation would be happening at a punk rock show.

They discuss what automation training should include and what certifications look like for different roles. Christelle also talks about how manufacturers can prepare the existing workforce for new opportunities, and how educators can help students connect with automation.

In this episode, find out:

  • How stackable credentials let working adults build their skills without taking years away from work
  • Why hands-on equipment time and simulation still matter as more training moves online
  • How manufacturers can upskill the workers they already have, and why tying training to a pay increase or promotion matters
  • How colleges work with local employers to shape their programs, and where apprenticeships fit into the picture
  • What A3 is doing to connect students with manufacturing through competitions, mentorship and the Education Pavilion at Automate
  • What Christelle hopes the future of automation will look like, and why she sees a national strategy as part of the picture

Enjoying the show? Please leave us a review here. Even one sentence helps. It’s feedback from Manufacturing All-Stars like you that keeps us going!

Tweetable Quotes:

  • “Nothing beats hands-on training and actually getting your hands onto the software and onto the equipment.” - Christelle Keefer, Director of Training and Certification at the Association for Advancing Automation
  • “Teachers who are bold and brave with technology learn with their students. They make mistakes with their students.” - Christelle Keefer, Director of Training and Certification at the Association for Advancing Automation
  • “Training tied to one brand doesn’t always transfer when someone changes jobs.” - Christelle Keefer, Director of Training and Certification at the Association for Advancing Automation

Links & mentions:

  • Association for Advancing Automation (A3) is North America’s largest automation trade association, representing more than 1,500 organizations involved in robotics, AI, machine vision, motion control and related technologies.
  • Automate is A3’s automation show, with an education pavilion, student robotics competitions, and a list of employers hiring on the floor.
  • Fathom Digital Manufacturing offers more than 25 advanced manufacturing technologies under one roof, from CNC machining to injection molding.

Make sure to visit http://manufacturinghappyhour.com for detailed show notes and a full list of resources mentioned in this episode. Stay Innovative, Stay Thirsty.
